correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, the S_n action preserves all coordinate ℓp norms. Any S_n-equivariant H-to-edge map has array entries a*x_i+b*x_j and therefore image inside cut space, annihilating both equivariant cross-maps with its orthogonal cycle complement. Group averaging makes Euclidean orthogonal projections minimal for every p. The graph Laplacian splits into eigenvalues n,n-2,2(n-1), yielding an exact five-orbit column partition with nonambiguous signs and an exact ℓ1 column sum 3-4/n. Since Q=I-P and the diagonal is (2n-1)/(n(n-1)), Q has the stated norm. Real symmetry gives endpoint ∞ norms. Independent exact rational and pseudoinverse finite checks corroborated every tested column. Earlier K_nn projections computed analogously give explicit gaps and threshold.

value.rationale: A dense graph obtained by deleting a perfect matching is a canonical complementability test of finite Lipschitz-free and transportation-cycle subspaces. The result computes exact unrestricted projection minima for every crown size (new range n>=5), proves both best norms respond strictly to the deletion despite retaining high symmetry, and identifies a one-dimension shift in which complementary space is harder to project onto. These are natural infinite-family structural and quantitative boundary results, not an arbitrary graph invariant, while known n=3,4 endpoints are not presented as novel.
